title: Viking Sky: near-grounding control for marine state-legibility and correction-infusion pattern
summary: Viking Sky is encoded as a near-miss/intercepted-control record: a cruise ship lost propulsion and steering in a storm and came within a ship length of grounding with 1,374 persons aboard, but did not become a mass-casualty loss; this calibrates the marine pattern against learning only from fatal accidents.

status_history.note: Added as near-miss/intercepted control for MKH-PAT-0023.

claims.claim: The NSIA page says Viking Sky experienced a blackout causing loss of propulsion and steering during a storm, came within a ship length of running aground, had 1,374 persons aboard, and had potential to become one of the worst modern disasters at sea.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NSIA page attributes the blackout to insufficient lube oil in operating diesel-generator sump tanks in combination with pitching/rolling and records non-compliant sump-tank design, missing dynamic-inclination operating limits, monitoring, and alarm-system recommendations.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: As a control record, Viking Sky shows that the marine state-divergence family includes near-misses and prevented/intercepted losses, not only fatal casualties; no claim is made here about the effectiveness of every recommendation.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: near-miss control status and limits encoded in record

type_payload.fit_rationale: Same broad factor family as marine casualty lane—propulsion/engineering state, dynamic sea-state/inclination, state visibility, alarm/monitoring design, passenger-vessel consequence exposure—but outcome was near-grounding rather than mass-casualty loss.
limits: Not a controlled success proof; the report still identifies serious design, operational, and organizational safety issues.
Does not prove recommendation implementation or industry-wide correction infusion.
Not a general statement about cruise-ship safety.

handling_notes: Marine-casualty records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not collapse safety-investigation causal language into individual blame; separate safety investigation, legal liability, vessel operation, design, maintenance, and emergency-response surfaces.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational navigation, stability, damage-control, legal, regulatory, or emergency guidance.

unknowns: Full NSIA PDF and recommendation status not extracted.
